newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Basis weakens on lack of demand.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Basis weakens on lack of demand.

text.p: Basis bids for hard red winter wheat in the High Plains were weaker at almost every location on Monday amid sluggish demand from both the export and domestic markets, grain dealers said.
They noted many Kansas mills had cut their basis bids between eight and 11 cents a bushel, depending on protein levels.
"The mills have pretty good coverage. I think we are moving towards new crop levels," one dealer said.
Export demand was also slow, contributing to weakness in U.S. Gulf bids. In Galveston, Texas, the basis was down five cents at 40 cents over May KCBT futures.
